findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The PIC’s Certified Food Protection Manager certificate expired in 2025 and they have not renewed it. The PIC stated that they will work on taking the CFPM test again to renew it. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on duty during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler shelves. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: There were pieces of food in the drain of the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing. CORRECTED- The sink was cleaned and the operators were educated. 

(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
(P) 2-301.11 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handle of paper towel dispenser was touched after handwashing process was completed to obtain paper towels. Handwashing technique was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands properly for remainder of inspection. Educational handout showing proper handwashing process was provided. Best practice would be to have paper towels ready prior to beginning handwashing process, but elbows and forearms may also be used to touch the handle and dispense paper towels. Ensure proper handwashing occurs between tasks and prior to food preparation and service. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
(P) 3-501.16 (A)(1) Top layer of meatballs in food warmer was observed with internal temperatures of 121F-126F. Meatballs further down in the container had internal temperatures at 145F-147F. Meatballs were heated in the microwave prior to placing in warmer. Meatballs were placed back in the microwave and later observed with an internal temperature of 165F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
(c) 6-501.111 Gnats were observed in the bag used for storage of soiled wiping cloths. Bag was immediately closed to keep gnats from getting out and removed from the area. Pest control options were discussed. Consider providing a sealed container and/or sealing used wiping cloths in a bag to minimize harborage. Gnats were not observed anywhere else in the facility.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
(c) 3-304.12 Ice scoop was observed on ledge of ice machine. Proper storage and protection from potential cross contamination were discussed. Pan was provided for storage of ice scoop.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is not TCS food.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
(c) 4-903.11 Food contact surfaces of soup spoons were presented out in a cup used for storage and intermixed with other spoons that had handles presented out. Proper storage was discussed, and spoons were repositioned so all utensils had the handles presented out. Ensure utensils are stored so only handles will be touched when retrieving.
Single service and single use articles shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of food-and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.12: (A) Observed interior cavity of microwave on food prep line to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize interior cavity of microwave. The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.
